source.paraphrase: Modules in one process still hide their internals. Callers use the published interface. Persistence and internal helpers stay inside the module that owns them.

invariants.why: A modular monolith stays one deployable only while modules meet at their public API. Crossing into internals couples two modules' private schemas.
invariants.fixHint: Call the other module through the function or type it exports from its root. Keep persistence inside the owning module.
invariants.avoid: export { row } from the other module's persistence path is still a cross-module edge.

source.work: Domain-Driven Design (E. Evans, 2003); Modular Monolith (K. Grzybek)
source.paraphrase: The shared module, if it exists, does not depend on any business module. Others may depend on it; it depends on none, staying free of business domain models.

invariants.why: A shared module that imports business modules creates circular dependencies and entangles shared utilities with specific domain logic.
invariants.fixHint: Remove business feature imports from shared code, or move the domain-specific logic into the owning module.
invariants.avoid: Re-exporting feature types or dynamically importing business modules from within shared/common packages.
